meta.title: RootLens sample (v0.1)
meta.description: 48 first-person clips of household tasks with per-frame 3D hand pose and natural-language action labels. ~1 GB. LeRobotDataset v3.0.

sample.pageIntro: Sample sets to verify the format and quality of data captured with the RootLens iOS app. New versions will be added as recording conditions and contributor scale expand.
sample.heroSubtitle: 48 first-person video clips of household tasks with per-frame 3D hand pose, wrist 6-DoF actions, and natural-language action labels.
sample.s1p1Lead: 48 clips of household tasks recorded with the RootLens iOS app from a head-mounted camera in Japan. All faces are blurred. Each frame contains:
s1p1Items: 21 hand joints in 3D per hand, in MANO canonical hand-local coordinates (`observation.hand_keypoints_3d`)
`task_index` into `meta/tasks.jsonl` pointing to a natural-language action label
sample.s2p1: LeRobotDataset v3.0 format. Standard loaders read this layout without modification.
sample.s3p1: Each frame's `task_index` maps to an action label in `meta/tasks.jsonl`. Labels are present-tense English sentences describing hand movements and objects (e.g. "Right hand reaches for the kettle handle."). Each clip is segmented into multiple labels at action transitions.
sample.s3p2: Labels are generated from video frames by a vision-language model.
sample.episodesSubheading: All 48 episodes. Click to play; expand a panel to read every action label with its timestamp.
sample.s4p1Lead: The next sample will add captures from roughly a dozen Japan-based TestFlight beta contributors:
s4p1Items: `observation.state` : camera 6-DoF in the ARKit world frame
`depth/{frame_index:06d}.png` : LiDAR depth maps on supported devices

hero.tagline: Hands-on footage from real workplaces, made robot-ready.
hero.description: RootLens is a University of Osaka-born data company. We collect first-person video of people at work and deliver it to teams building physical AI, turning real kitchens and shops into training data robots can learn from.

problem.title: Robots learn by watching people. The footage is the bottleneck.
problem.p1: Robot intelligence is advancing at a startling pace. AI has moved from language to vision, and now to physical motion. Robots are learning how to move by watching humans work.
problem.p2: Yet high-quality footage of real work in real places is scarce. The traditional approach, staging demonstrations in a lab, is expensive, slow, and misses the messiness of reality.
problem.p3: Human motion footage is the bottleneck. RootLens collects it where people actually work.

appFlow.title: The workplace becomes the collection site

step1.label: Work as usual
step1.text: Staff wearing a head-mounted camera work normal part-time shifts. Dishwashing, prep work, the usual jobs, unchanged.

step2.label: Data while working
step2.text: First-person video plus depth, motion, and hand-pose data from each shift becomes training material for robot manipulation.

step3.label: Stores get paid back
step3.text: We pay stores a filming fee for every recorded hour, so they keep the extra hands while their effective labor cost goes down.

issues.title: Why this data is valuable
issues.intro1: Robotics teams cannot train on random video. They need task-focused, hands-visible footage shot in real environments, across as many different sites as possible.
issues.intro2: RootLens data comes from real kitchens, real shops, real homes. Different layouts, different tools, different habits. That diversity is the value.
issues.pillarsLead: Every clip in the dataset meets four conditions.

hands.label: First-person, hands-first
hands.text: How things are grasped, moved, and handled with tools. Head-mounted cameras capture exactly what robots need to learn manipulation.

sensors.label: More than video
sensors.text: RGB video recorded together with LiDAR depth, IMU motion, and hand pose, so space and movement can be reconstructed in 3D.

diversity.label: Real-world diversity
diversity.text: Unstaged workplaces with real lighting and real clutter, a breadth of distribution lab collection cannot reach.

consent.label: Consent-backed provenance
consent.text: Written agreements with every site, faces blurred, no audio recorded, and a consent record linked to every clip.
